subject.title: [Bug] WebChat: optimistic USER messages are lost (not just hidden) when chat.send returns before the durable transcript lands — full-replace history reconcile drops them

question: Should WebChat `chat.send` return `started` only after the user turn is durably recorded, or should it keep the faster ACK and add explicit visible recovery/failure semantics for unpersisted turns?
rationale: Current source proves the ACK-before-recorder boundary remains, but the best product contract affects latency, duplicate suppression, and how session recovery reports failures.

options.title: Persist Before ACK
options.body: Make durable user-turn persistence part of a successful `chat.send` ACK and return a terminal failure when that cannot be established.

options.title: Fast ACK With Recovery
options.body: Keep the low-latency ACK but add a durable pending/recovery state and a visible failure if persistence or dispatch never completes.

options.title: Close As UI Mitigated
options.body: Treat the current pending-send and optimistic-history preservation as sufficient and leave the gateway ACK contract unchanged.

recommendation.title: Persist Before ACK
recommendation.body: Make durable user-turn persistence part of a successful `chat.send` ACK and return a terminal failure when that cannot be established.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision lives on the shared user-turn recorder and gateway fallback persistence contract introduced in the transcript centralization work.
